traditions.name: Friday Night Planetarium Show
traditions.description: The Wayne State Planetarium in Old Main puts on free public shows most Friday evenings, with a tour of the current night sky and a fulldome film. Arrive early, since seats are first come, first served.

traditions.name: Old Main's Peregrine Falcons
traditions.description: Peregrine falcons live on a balcony of Old Main's clock tower, and the university calls them its winged Warriors. Look up at the tower to spot them.

traditions.name: Campus ArtWalk
traditions.description: Around 30 donated outdoor sculptures make the campus an open-air gallery you can visit any time. Start at "City with Halo" in front of the Thompson Home and follow the ArtWalk map.

traditions.name: Homecoming Game at Tom Adams Field
traditions.description: Homecoming week ends with Warrior football at Tom Adams Field, and fans are asked to wear green and gold. Join the crowd and cheer on the Warriors.

details.airportInfo: Detroit Metropolitan Wayne County Airport in Romulus, southwest of Detroit, is Michigan's busiest airport and the main gateway to the city.
details.funFact: Old Main, the clock-towered heart of campus, was built in the 1890s as Detroit's Central High School. College classes that started there grew into Wayne State University.
details.languageInfo: The school colors are green and gold, and the teams are the Warriors.
details.transportationFact: The main campus in Midtown is easy to walk. The QLINE streetcar runs along Woodward Avenue at the campus's east edge and links it with Downtown Detroit and New Center.

buildings.name: Old Main
buildings.description: Malcomson & Higginbotham designed this brick and limestone landmark as Detroit's Central High School, which began classes here in 1896. Its clock tower still marks the corner of Cass and Warren.

buildings.name: McGregor Memorial Conference Center
buildings.description: Minoru Yamasaki's travertine-clad pavilion, completed in 1958, sits beside a reflecting pool and sunken garden under a skylit hall. It is a National Historic Landmark for its architecture.

buildings.name: Maccabees Building
buildings.description: Albert Kahn designed this 15-story Art Deco tower on Woodward Avenue, finished in 1927. Also called Wayne Tower, it is now owned by Wayne State.

buildings.name: Charles Lang Freer House
buildings.description: Wilson Eyre designed this Shingle-style house in 1892 for art collector Charles Lang Freer, whose gift founded the Smithsonian's Freer Gallery of Art. It now houses Wayne State's Merrill Palmer Skillman Institute.

buildings.name: Hilberry Theatre
buildings.description: Built in 1917 as the First Church of Christ, Scientist, this Neoclassical building became Wayne State's graduate theatre in 1963. It is being renovated as the Gretchen C. Valade Jazz Center.

buildings.name: Hilberry Gateway
buildings.description: This performing arts center opened in April 2023 next to the old Hilberry Theatre. Its 550-seat proscenium theater is home to the university's theatre and dance productions.

buildings.name: Walter P. Reuther Library
buildings.description: O'Dell, Hewlett and Luckenbach designed this home for the largest labor archives in North America, completed in 1975. It is named for UAW president Walter Reuther.

buildings.name: David Adamany Undergraduate Library
buildings.description: Built in 1997 at the center of Gullen Mall, this is one of Wayne State's largest libraries, with more than 2,000 seats. It is named for the university's eighth president, David Adamany.

traditions.name: The Bronco Statue
traditions.description: A 1,800-pound bronze bronco by sculptor Veryl Goodnight has stood on campus since 1997. It was first part of her larger work "The Day the Wall Came Down." Snap a photo with it.

traditions.name: Homecoming at Waldo Stadium
traditions.description: Each October WMU paints the town brown and gold for Homecoming, ending with Broncos football at Waldo Stadium. Join the crowd in the stands.

traditions.name: National Champions at Lawson Arena
traditions.description: The Broncos won their first men's ice hockey national championship in 2025. Catch a game at Lawson Arena and look for the championship banner.

traditions.name: Up Prospect Hill to Heritage Hall
traditions.description: WMU began on Prospect Hill, where East Hall opened in 1905 and a trolley once carried people up the slope. Walk up to Heritage Hall, the restored East Hall, and the North Hall portico beside it.

details.airportInfo: Kalamazoo/Battle Creek International Airport, southeast of downtown Kalamazoo, is the nearest airport with airline service.
details.funFact: Hyames Field, WMU's baseball park on East Campus, hosted the very first College World Series in 1947 and again in 1948.
details.languageInfo: The school colors are brown and gold, and the teams are the Broncos.
details.transportationFact: Kalamazoo's Metro buses serve Western Michigan University as well as the city and its suburbs.

buildings.name: Heritage Hall (East Hall)
buildings.description: East Hall, the first building of the Western State Normal School, opened on Prospect Hill in 1905. After its wings came down in 2013, the original core reopened in 2015 as Heritage Hall, home of the WMU Alumni Center.

buildings.name: Miller Auditorium
buildings.description: Opened in 1968 and named for WMU's third president, James W. Miller, this 3,497-seat hall is the fifth-largest auditorium in Michigan. Touring Broadway shows and the Kalamazoo Symphony Orchestra perform here.

buildings.name: Richmond Center for Visual Arts
buildings.description: Opened in 2007, this arts center houses part of the Frostic School of Art. Its first floor holds three galleries for rotating shows, the university art collection and student work.

buildings.name: Waldo Stadium
buildings.description: Broncos football has played on this East Campus site since 1914, and the full stadium opened in 1939. It is named for Dwight B. Waldo, the school's first president, and seats 30,200.

buildings.name: Hyames Field
buildings.description: Built in 1939 alongside Waldo Stadium, this baseball park hosted the first College World Series in 1947 and the second in 1948. It is home to Broncos baseball.

buildings.name: University Arena (Read Fieldhouse)
buildings.description: Read Fieldhouse opened in 1957 and is named for longtime basketball coach Buck Read. A 1994 renovation turned the floor 90 degrees and created the 5,421-seat University Arena.

buildings.name: Lawson Arena
buildings.description: This horseshoe-shaped, 3,667-seat ice arena opened in 1974 for Broncos hockey. Its old-style design and loud fans make it one of the toughest rinks for visiting teams.

buildings.name: John E. Fetzer Center
buildings.description: Opened in 1983, this conference center is named for radio pioneer and Detroit Tigers owner John Fetzer. Its lounge has an exhibit on his life.

traditions.name: Little Mac Bridge and the Ravines
traditions.description: Students voted the ravines and the Little Mac Bridge the most beautiful spot on campus. Cross the footbridge and look down at the stream below.

traditions.name: Carillon Music at Cook Tower
traditions.description: Every week the university carillonist plays music, from Bach to pop songs, on the bells of the Cook Carillon Tower. If you hear bells, someone is up there playing live.

traditions.name: Zumberge Pond
traditions.description: Lakers love to study, eat or just relax on the steps beside Zumberge Pond in any season. Take a seat and enjoy the view.

traditions.name: View from the Library Roof
traditions.description: The roof of the Mary Idema Pew Library gives a sweeping view of the Allendale campus, a student favorite when the leaves change in fall. Go up and take in the view.

traditions.name: Laker Football at Lubbers Stadium
traditions.description: Lubbers Stadium officially seats 10,444 but often holds thousands more fans, with a record crowd of 17,007 in 2021. Join them for a Lakers home game.

details.airportInfo: Gerald R. Ford International Airport, southeast of Grand Rapids, is the nearest airport with airline service.
details.funFact: Grand Valley is one of only three institutions in the Western Hemisphere with more than one carillon tower: the Cook Carillon in Allendale and the Beckering Family Carillon in Grand Rapids.
details.languageInfo: The school colors are blue, black and white, and the teams are the Lakers.
details.transportationFact: The Laker Line bus, run by The Rapid, links the Allendale campus with GVSU's campuses in downtown Grand Rapids along Lake Michigan Drive, and it is open to the public.

buildings.name: Cook Carillon Tower
buildings.description: This 10-story brick and stone clock tower, finished in 1994, is the focal point of the Allendale campus. Its 48 bronze bells were cast by the Royal Eijsbouts foundry in the Netherlands.

buildings.name: Kirkhof Center
buildings.description: Dedicated in 1974 as the Campus Center, the student union was renamed for Russel H. Kirkhof in 1984. It holds dining, meeting rooms and student offices, and the Laker Line bus stops outside.

buildings.name: Mary Idema Pew Library
buildings.description: SHW Group designed this library, which opened in June 2013 as the intellectual heart of the Allendale campus. It was the first library in Michigan to earn LEED Platinum certification.

buildings.name: Lubbers Stadium
buildings.description: Opened in 1973 as Lakers Stadium and later named for president Arend Lubbers, this is the home of Grand Valley football. It seats 10,444 and drew a record 17,007 fans in 2021.

buildings.name: GVSU Fieldhouse Arena
buildings.description: Opened in 1982 after the roof of the old "Dome" was condemned, this 4,200-seat arena is home to Lakers basketball and volleyball. It also hosts commencement and concerts.
buildings.address: Grand Valley State University, Allendale, MI 49401

traditions.name: Ypsilanti Water Tower
traditions.description: Built in 1890 on the highest point in Ypsilanti, the stone water tower borders the campus and is the city's best-known landmark. Locals give directions by it, so take a photo with it.

traditions.name: The Pray-Harrold Kiosk
traditions.description: Covering the kiosk outside Pray-Harrold with flyers for campus events is a longstanding Eastern tradition. Stop by and read what's happening this week.

traditions.name: Concert at Pease Auditorium
traditions.description: Pease Auditorium has been the campus concert hall since 1915. Catch a performance and listen for its 81-rank Aeolian-Skinner pipe organ.

traditions.name: The Ghost of Starkweather Hall
traditions.description: Campus legend says Mary Ann Starkweather, who paid for the hall, haunts it because it no longer serves the religious purpose she intended. Walk past the oldest building on campus and look up at its tower.

details.airportInfo: Detroit Metropolitan Wayne County Airport in Romulus, east of Ypsilanti, is the nearest major airport.
details.funFact: Founded in 1849 as the Michigan State Normal School, Eastern was the fourth teachers' college in the United States and the first outside New England.
details.languageInfo: The school colors are green and white, and the teams are the Eagles.
details.transportationFact: The main campus is compact and easy to walk. TheRide buses link Ypsilanti and the campus with Ann Arbor.

buildings.name: Starkweather Hall
buildings.description: Built in 1896 with a gift from Mary Ann Starkweather for the Students' Christian Association, this fieldstone building is the oldest on campus. When it opened, it was the only religious center at any teachers' college in the country.

buildings.name: Pease Auditorium
buildings.description: Smith, Hinchman & Grylls designed this concert hall, dedicated in 1915 in memory of music professor Frederic H. Pease. Its 81-rank Aeolian-Skinner organ was installed in the early 1960s and restored in the late 1990s.

buildings.name: Sherzer Hall
buildings.description: E. W. Arnold of Battle Creek designed this 1903 science building, which has survived two fires. The Sherzer Observatory sits on top, and the building is now home to the art department.

buildings.name: McKenny Hall
buildings.description: Opened in 1931 as Charles McKenny Union, this was the campus's first student union. Over the years it held a bowling alley, a ballroom and bookstores; today it houses offices and a Chick-fil-A.

buildings.name: Bruce T. Halle Library
buildings.description: Opened in 1998, the four-story library is named for EMU graduate Bruce T. Halle, founder of Discount Tire. Most of its books are kept in an automated retrieval system several stories below the building.

buildings.name: Eastern Michigan University Student Center
buildings.description: Opened in 2006, the four-floor Student Center replaced McKenny Union as the hub of campus life. It stands in University Park near the library.

buildings.name: Bowen Field House
buildings.description: Opened in 1955, this 6,000-seat field house was home to Eagles basketball until the Convocation Center opened in the late 1990s. It still hosts track and field, wrestling and gymnastics.

traditions.name: Winter Carnival Snow Statues
traditions.description: Every February since the 1930s, students pile, stomp and carve snow into giant statues on a yearly theme for Winter Carnival, which began in 1922. Walk the campus and see them.

traditions.name: Huskies Pep Band at a Hockey Game
traditions.description: The Huskies Pep Band, formed in 1928, plays at every home hockey game. Join the crowd in linking arms and swaying to the "Blue Skirt Waltz", the Copper Country Anthem.

traditions.name: The Giant Copper Boulder
traditions.description: The Copper Pavilion outside the A. E. Seaman Mineral Museum holds a 19-ton boulder of copper pulled from the bottom of Lake Superior, a Guinness World Record holder. Go see how big it is.

traditions.name: A Show at the Rozsa Center
traditions.description: The Rozsa Center for the Performing Arts hosts film and music festivals through the year, including the Pine Mountain Music Festival and the 41 North Film Festival. Check the calendar and catch a show.

details.airportInfo: Houghton County Memorial Airport, north of Hancock across Portage Lake, is the nearest airport with airline service.
details.funFact: Founded in 1885 as the Michigan Mining School, Michigan Tech was the first college in Michigan's Upper Peninsula. Houghton gets about 218 inches (5.5 m) of snow in an average year.
details.languageInfo: The school colors are black and gold, and the teams are the Huskies.
details.transportationFact: The main part of campus sits on a bluff above Portage Lake along US-41 and can be crossed on foot in about 10 minutes.

buildings.name: College Club House and Gymnasium
buildings.description: Built in 1904, this English Tudor Revival building is the oldest standing building on Michigan Tech's campus. Also known as the ROTC Building, it was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1980.

buildings.name: Memorial Union Building
buildings.description: Alumni raised $300,000 toward this student union, finished in 1952 and named in tribute to Michigan Tech people who served in the armed forces. Renovated in 1987, it holds dining, a bookstore, lounges and game rooms.

buildings.name: A. E. Seaman Mineral Museum
buildings.description: Michigan's official mineral museum began in 1902 and moved into its own new building, Thomas D. Shaffner Hall, in 2011. It holds more than 36,000 specimens, many from the Lake Superior region.

buildings.name: MacInnes Student Ice Arena
buildings.description: Opened in January 1972, the home of Huskies hockey is named for John MacInnes, who coached the team from 1956 to 1983 with a record of 555-295-39. Spring commencement is held here too.

traditions.name: Summer Carillon Concerts
traditions.description: On six Fridays each summer, carillonneurs from around the world give free concerts on the 49 bells of Elliott Tower. Come and listen from the lawn around the tower.

traditions.name: Rub the Grizz
traditions.description: Students rub the belly of the 8-foot bronze grizzly outside the O'rena for luck before a big exam. Give it a rub and take a photo.

traditions.name: Holiday Walk at Meadow Brook Hall
traditions.description: Each holiday season, Meadow Brook Hall is decorated for its Holiday Walk, and Winter Wonder Lights fill the grounds at night. Plan a visit to see the mansion dressed for the season.

traditions.name: Summer Concert at Meadow Brook
traditions.description: Meadow Brook Amphitheatre has hosted summer concerts on campus since 1964. Catch a show from a pavilion seat or out on the lawn.

details.airportInfo: Detroit Metropolitan Wayne County Airport in Romulus, southwest of Detroit, is the main airport for the area, about an hour's drive from campus.
details.funFact: Oakland was founded in 1957 with a gift from Matilda Dodge Wilson and her husband Alfred, including their Meadow Brook estate. Their 110-room mansion, Meadow Brook Hall, still stands on campus.
details.languageInfo: The school colors are black and gold, and the teams are the Golden Grizzlies.
details.transportationFact: The main campus spans Auburn Hills and Rochester Hills. Meadow Brook Hall and the John Dodge House are on the east side, about 1 to 2 km from Elliott Tower.

buildings.name: Elliott Tower
buildings.description: A gift from Hugh and Nancy Elliott, this 151-foot carillon tower was dedicated in September 2014 as the centerpiece of the main campus. A fountain and a garden surround its base.

buildings.name: Meadow Brook Hall
buildings.description: Matilda Dodge Wilson and her second husband, lumber baron Alfred Wilson, built this 110-room Tudor Revival mansion between 1926 and 1929. It is now a National Historic Landmark and one of the largest historic house museums in the country.
buildings.architect: William E. Kapp; Smith, Hinchman & Grylls

buildings.name: John Dodge House
buildings.description: This farmhouse was built in 1898, and automaker John F. Dodge and his wife Matilda bought it in 1908 as a weekend retreat, growing it from 14 to 30 rooms. It now holds university offices.

buildings.name: Meadow Brook Amphitheatre
buildings.description: Opened in 1964 as the Meadow Brook Music Festival, this outdoor music venue seats 7,701: 2,819 under the pavilion roof and the rest on the lawn.

buildings.name: OU Credit Union O'rena
buildings.description: Opened in November 1998, the 4,000-seat arena is home to Golden Grizzlies basketball and volleyball. It is nicknamed "The Blacktop" for the black court first used in the 2015-16 season.

traditions.name: Fire Up, Chips!
traditions.description: "Fire Up, Chips!" is Central's greeting and rallying cry. At a football game at Kelly/Shorts Stadium, jingle your keys before big plays and mime crashing cymbals with the crowd.

traditions.name: Warriner Hall Chimes
traditions.description: Chimes have sounded from Warriner Hall since 1939, and today recorded chimes greet each new hour. Stand on Warriner Mall and listen for them on the hour.

traditions.name: Cardboard Boat Race
traditions.description: On Homecoming morning, engineering students try to paddle boats made of cardboard across the Rose Ponds. Find a spot on the bank and cheer them on.

traditions.name: Celebrating Life Pow Wow
traditions.description: Each March, Central hosts the Celebrating Life Pow Wow in McGuirk Arena, with traditional dancing, drumming, arts and food. It is open to the public, so come and watch.

details.airportInfo: MBS International Airport in Freeland, east of Mount Pleasant, is the nearest airport with airline service.
details.funFact: Kelly/Shorts Stadium, with 35,127 seats, is the largest on-campus stadium in the Mid-American Conference.
details.languageInfo: The school colors are maroon and gold, and the teams are the Chippewas.
details.transportationFact: The campus is easy to walk: Warriner Hall on the north side is about 1.5 km from Kelly/Shorts Stadium in the southeast.

buildings.name: Warriner Hall
buildings.description: Built where Old Main stood before it burned in 1925, this building opened in 1928 as the Administration Building, with the library in its east wing. It was named for president Eugene C. Warriner when he retired in 1939.
buildings.address: Central Michigan University, Mount Pleasant, MI 48859

buildings.name: Charles V. Park Library
buildings.description: Named for longtime library director Charles V. Park, the library opened in 1969 and reopened in 2002 after it was enlarged to more than 300,000 square feet. The Clarke Historical Library, with rare books and Michigan history, is on its first floor.
buildings.address: Central Michigan University, Mount Pleasant, MI 48859

buildings.name: Brooks Astronomical Observatory
buildings.description: Set up in 1964 on the roof of the Brooks Hall science building, the observatory is named for Kendall P. Brooks, who taught astronomy here from 1910 to 1947. Its 16-inch telescope dates from 1996.
buildings.address: Brooks Hall, Central Michigan University, Mount Pleasant, MI 48859

buildings.name: Kelly/Shorts Stadium
buildings.description: Opened in 1972 and enlarged since, the home of Chippewas football seats 35,127, the most of any on-campus stadium in the Mid-American Conference. Its field is named for former coaches Roy Kramer and Herb Deromedi.
buildings.address: 2300 E Campus Dr, Mount Pleasant, MI 48858

buildings.name: McGuirk Arena
buildings.description: Opened in 1973 as Rose Arena, this arena is home to Chippewas basketball, gymnastics, volleyball and wrestling. It is part of the larger CMU Events Center.
buildings.address: Central Michigan University, Mount Pleasant, MI 48859
